newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Generali executives in Israel for fence-mending.
newsitem.headline: Generali executives in Israel for fence-mending.

text.p: Senior officials of Italian insurer Generali SpA met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday in a fence-mending visit following controversy over policies held by Holocaust victims.

A statement issued by Generali said the visit by managing director Gianfranco Gutty and two other top officials had "put to rest" troubles surrounding its $320 million investment in Israel's Leumi Insurance Holdings.
Generali had faced threats from Israeli legislators of a boycott unless it honoured insurance policies held by European Jews killed in the Nazi Holocaust.

The Italian insurer said it was not legally liable for claims from victims' relatives on policies held in Central and Eastern Europe, where its businesses were expropriated by communist governments after World War Two.

But Generali subsequently announced last month it had set up a $12 million fund for ex gratia payments to beneficiaries in accordance with criteria to be determined by a committee headed by a retired justice of the Israeli Supreme Court.

The company is one of seven European insurance firms against which a massive U.S. lawsuit was filed in March. The class action suit, combining the claims of an estimated 10,000 plaintiffs, accuses the seven firms of cheating Holocaust victims of billions of dollars.

The other firms are Wiener Allianz Verischerungs Aktiengesellschaft of Vienna, A.G.F. Assurances Generales de France Vie of Paris, Riunione Adriatica Di Sicurta S.p.A. of Milan, Allianz Group of Munich, Der Anker Allgemeine Versicherungs AG of Vienna, and Bavarian Reinsurance Co of Munich.
Generali said it is in the process of computerising information regarding policies held during the war.
"A policy information centre is being established by Generali for individuals seeking information regarding policies held in Central and Eastern Europe during this era," the Generali statement said.
"An 800 phone number will be activated in the United States for access to the information centre," it added.
